objectives.title: Identify typical test objectives
Differentiate testing from debugging
Exemplify why testing is necessary
Recall the relation between testing and quality assurance
Distinguish between root cause, error, defect, and failure
Explain the seven testing principles
Explain the different test activities and related tasks
Explain the impact of context on the test process
Differentiate the testware that supports the test activities
Explain the value of maintaining traceability
Compare the different roles in testing
Give examples of the generic skills required for testing
Recall the advantages of the whole team approach
Distinguish the benefits and drawbacks of independence of testing
Explain the impact of the chosen software development lifecycle on testing
Recall good testing practices that apply to all software development lifecycles
Recall the examples of test-first approaches to development
Summarize how DevOps might have an impact on testing
Explain shift left
Explain how retrospectives can be used as a mechanism for process improvement
Distinguish the different test levels
Distinguish the different test types
Distinguish confirmation testing from regression testing
Summarize maintenance testing and its triggers
Recognize types of work products that can be examined by static testing
Explain the value of static testing
Compare and contrast static testing and dynamic testing
Identify the benefits of early and frequent stakeholder feedback
Summarize the activities of the review process
Recall which responsibilities are assigned to the principal roles when performing reviews
Compare and contrast the different review types
Recall the factors that contribute to a successful review
Distinguish black- box test techniques, white-box test techniques and experience-based test techniques
Use equivalence partitioning to derive test cases
Use boundary value analysis to derive test cases
Use decision table testing to derive test cases
Use state transition testing to derive test cases
Explain statement testing
Explain branch testing
Explain the value of white-box testing
Explain error guessing
Explain exploratory testing
Explain checklist-based testing
Explain how to write user stories in collaboration with developers and business representatives
Classify the different options for writing acceptance criteria
Use acceptance test-driven development (ATDD) to derive test cases
Exemplify the purpose and content of a test plan
Recognize how a tester adds value to iteration and release planning
Compare and contrast entry criteria and exit criteria
Use estimation techniques to calculate the required test effort
Apply test case prioritization
Recall the concepts of the test pyramid
Summarize the testing quadrants and their relationships with test levels and test types
Identify risk level by using risk likelihood and risk impact
Distinguish between project risks and product risks
Explain how product risk analysis may influence thoroughness and test scope
Explain what measures can be taken in response to analyzed product risks
Recall metrics used for testing
Summarize the purposes, content, and audiences for test reports
Exemplify how to communicate the status of testing
Summarize how configuration management supports testing
Prepare a defect report
Explain how different types of test tools support testing
Recall the benefits and risks of test automation

questions.prompt: HOP is about to release a new permissions screen. Which is a valid test objective?
options: Guarantee every possible input is tested
Evaluate whether access rules are met
Prove no future failures are possible
questions.explanation: Testing supplies information and reduces risk; it cannot prove the absence of every defect.

questions.prompt: A banking release has limited test time. What useful result can testing provide?
options: Proof that all users will be satisfied
Elimination of the need for monitoring
Evidence about quality and remaining risk
questions.explanation: Testing supplies information and reduces risk; it cannot prove the absence of every defect.

questions.prompt: A HOP test exposes duplicate notifications; a developer locates and fixes the faulty loop. Which activity is debugging?
options: Executing the test that exposed duplicates
questions.explanation: Testing reveals defects or failures; debugging diagnoses causes and removes defects.

questions.prompt: A tester reproduces a checkout failure and a developer repairs the calculation. Which description is correct?
options: Reproduction is testing; diagnosis and repair are debugging
questions.explanation: Testing reveals defects or failures; debugging diagnoses causes and removes defects.

questions.prompt: Why test HOP role restrictions before launch even when developers are experienced?
options: An unnoticed defect could expose manager actions to staff
Experienced developers cannot test their own work
Testing guarantees no unauthorized use ever
questions.explanation: Testing helps uncover defects and informs decisions about quality and risk.

questions.prompt: A hospital team tests a familiar workflow after a platform change. Why is this worthwhile?
options: Testing removes the need for a release decision
Prior successful use proves the new platform works
It can expose failures before patients depend on the change
questions.explanation: Testing helps uncover defects and informs decisions about quality and risk.

questions.prompt: Which activity is primarily quality assurance?
options: Improving the team's review process to prevent recurring mistakes
Comparing actual and expected API results
questions.explanation: QA is process-oriented and preventive; testing evaluates work products as quality control.

questions.prompt: Which pairing best describes QA and testing?
options: QA fixes code; testing writes requirements
QA and testing are always identical
Testing prevents all defects; QA finds all failures
QA improves processes; testing evaluates products
questions.explanation: QA is process-oriented and preventive; testing evaluates work products as quality control.

questions.prompt: A developer misunderstands a timezone rule, writes the wrong offset, and HOP displays the wrong shift time. What is the wrong offset in code?
questions.explanation: A human error can introduce a defect; executing that defect may cause a failure. A root cause is the underlying reason.

questions.prompt: A missing training process leads a person to misread a rule and implement a bad formula. What is the missing training process in this causal chain?
questions.explanation: A human error can introduce a defect; executing that defect may cause a failure. A root cause is the underlying reason.

questions.prompt: Every specified HOP feature passes, but managers cannot complete their real workflow. Which principle best explains the problem?
questions.explanation: Testing shows defects can exist, not that none remain. Exhaustive testing is generally impossible; tests must adapt and reflect user needs.

questions.prompt: A repeatedly reused suite finds fewer new defects. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Review and vary tests because tests wear out
Stop testing because the product is defect-free
Assume testing can never find new defects
questions.explanation: Testing shows defects can exist, not that none remain. Exhaustive testing is generally impossible; tests must adapt and reflect user needs.

questions.prompt: The HOP tester identifies which permissions need checking from the requirements. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: Analysis identifies testable features and conditions; design derives test cases; implementation prepares procedures and data.

questions.prompt: A tester turns checkout conditions into specific inputs and expected results. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: Analysis identifies testable features and conditions; design derives test cases; implementation prepares procedures and data.

questions.prompt: Should HOP use exactly the same test process as flight-control software?
options: No; risk and context change the appropriate process
Yes; all software needs identical formality
No; business software needs no tests
questions.explanation: Domain, risks, stakeholders, lifecycle, constraints and technology affect test activities and their formality.

questions.prompt: Two teams build a prototype and a regulated payment service. What should drive differences in testing?
questions.explanation: Domain, risks, stakeholders, lifecycle, constraints and technology affect test activities and their formality.

questions.prompt: Which HOP artifact is primarily produced during test execution?
options: A contract with the hosting provider
questions.explanation: Test conditions, cases, data, scripts, logs and reports support different testing activities.

questions.prompt: Which artifact helps test implementation prepare execution?
options: An ordered test procedure and test data
questions.explanation: Test conditions, cases, data, scripts, logs and reports support different testing activities.

questions.prompt: The HOP permission requirement changes. What makes affected tests easier to identify?
options: Sorting all defect reports by author
Links from requirements to test cases
questions.explanation: Traceability supports coverage evaluation, change impact analysis and clear status reporting.

questions.prompt: A stakeholder asks which requirements have passed testing. What provides the best evidence?
options: A list of tool license costs
The number of lines in the test plan
questions.explanation: Traceability supports coverage evaluation, change impact analysis and clear status reporting.

questions.prompt: A HOP lead reallocates test time after a high-risk defect appears. Which role is being performed?
questions.explanation: Test management coordinates planning and control; the testing role performs technical test activities. One person may hold both roles.

questions.prompt: A small team has one person plan testing and derive test cases. Is that consistent with the testing roles?
options: No; each role must be a separate department
No; testers cannot derive test cases
Only if no test plan is written
Yes; one person may perform both management and testing roles
questions.explanation: Test management coordinates planning and control; the testing role performs technical test activities. One person may hold both roles.

questions.prompt: A HOP requirement is ambiguous. What should the tester do first?
options: Silently assume the most convenient interpretation
Ask a clear question and discuss concrete examples
questions.explanation: Analytical thinking, curiosity, attention to detail and constructive communication help testing.

questions.prompt: A developer disputes a defect. Which response best supports collaboration?
options: Claim that testers never make mistakes
Share reproducible evidence and discuss expected behavior
questions.explanation: Analytical thinking, curiosity, attention to detail and constructive communication help testing.

questions.prompt: Who is responsible for quality under a whole team approach?
options: Only the last developer to commit
questions.explanation: People with the needed skills collaborate and share responsibility for quality; this does not remove specialist skills.

questions.prompt: What is a typical benefit of the whole team approach?
options: Eliminating all need for testing expertise
Using different skills together to improve quality
questions.explanation: People with the needed skills collaborate and share responsibility for quality; this does not remove specialist skills.

questions.prompt: Why have another person review HOP tests written by the developer?
options: Only independent people can execute tests
Different assumptions may expose missed defects
questions.explanation: Independent testers bring different assumptions, but separation can create communication barriers and reduce shared ownership.

questions.prompt: What is a potential drawback of a highly isolated test team?
options: A guaranteed increase in product quality
questions.explanation: Independent testers bring different assumptions, but separation can create communication barriers and reduce shared ownership.

questions.prompt: HOP moves from one large release to short iterations. How should testing adapt?
options: Test incrementally with frequent feedback and regression checks
Wait until all iterations are finished
questions.explanation: Lifecycle choices influence timing, scope, documentation and feedback; testing remains relevant across lifecycles.

questions.prompt: A sequential project reviews requirements before coding. Why is this appropriate?
options: Reviews replace every later dynamic test
Testing activities can begin before executable software exists
Testing is possible only after deployment
questions.explanation: Lifecycle choices influence timing, scope, documentation and feedback; testing remains relevant across lifecycles.

questions.prompt: Which practice applies across development lifecycles?
options: Use the same test level for every objective
Keep testers away from requirement discussions
Begin relevant test analysis and design early
Always postpone testing until coding ends
questions.explanation: Every development activity has a corresponding testing activity; analysis and design begin early and tests align with objectives.

questions.prompt: Which is a generally good testing practice?
options: Require every project to use identical documents
Associate development activities with appropriate testing activities
Remove test objectives to increase flexibility
questions.explanation: Every development activity has a corresponding testing activity; analysis and design begin early and tests align with objectives.

questions.prompt: Which set contains test-first development approaches?
questions.explanation: TDD, ATDD and BDD are test-first approaches with different emphases.

questions.prompt: Which approach expresses desired behavior in a form such as Given/When/Then before implementation?
questions.explanation: TDD, ATDD and BDD are test-first approaches with different emphases.

questions.prompt: HOP adds a CI pipeline. What is a realistic testing benefit?
options: Removal of all test maintenance costs
A guarantee every deployment is safe
Proof that exploratory testing is unnecessary
questions.explanation: DevOps supports collaboration, CI/CD and automated feedback but does not eliminate manual testing or risk.

questions.prompt: What testing challenge can DevOps introduce?
options: Maintaining reliable automated checks in a rapid pipeline
Removing the need for test environments
questions.explanation: DevOps supports collaboration, CI/CD and automated feedback but does not eliminate manual testing or risk.

questions.prompt: Which HOP action is an example of shift left?
options: Deleting system tests when unit tests pass
Waiting for customers to report access failures
questions.explanation: Shift left moves testing earlier, such as reviewing requirements and running early tests; later testing is still needed.

questions.prompt: A team introduces early API contract reviews. What should happen to later system testing?
options: Replace every test with a review checklist
Keep appropriate later tests; earlier reviews complement them
questions.explanation: Shift left moves testing earlier, such as reviewing requirements and running early tests; later testing is still needed.

questions.prompt: HOP's last release suffered unclear test data. What is the best retrospective outcome?
options: Assign an owner to improve data preparation and review the result
questions.explanation: Retrospectives identify improvements, assign actions and evaluate whether they work.

questions.prompt: How can a team tell whether a retrospective helped?
options: Count only how many people attended
Check whether agreed improvements were implemented and effective
questions.explanation: Retrospectives identify improvements, assign actions and evaluate whether they work.

questions.prompt: A HOP test checks how its API and PostgreSQL exchange a saved request. What is its main focus?
questions.explanation: Component tests focus on isolated parts; integration tests on interactions; system tests on the whole system; acceptance tests on business needs.

questions.prompt: Restaurant managers evaluate whether the complete ordering workflow meets their needs. Which level best fits?
questions.explanation: Component tests focus on isolated parts; integration tests on interactions; system tests on the whole system; acceptance tests on business needs.

questions.prompt: HOP loads a published schedule for 500 simultaneous users and measures response time. Which type best fits?
questions.explanation: Functional tests assess what the system does; non-functional tests assess quality characteristics such as performance or usability.

questions.prompt: A test checks whether a staff account is denied a manager-only action. What requirement is being tested?
questions.explanation: Functional tests assess what the system does; non-functional tests assess quality characteristics such as performance or usability.

questions.prompt: The availability bug is fixed. Testing shift swaps to detect unintended effects is what?
options: Confirmation of the original availability defect only
questions.explanation: Confirmation checks whether the original defect was fixed; regression checks unintended consequences elsewhere.

questions.prompt: A tester reruns the exact steps of a previously failing invoice calculation after its repair. What is the primary purpose?
questions.explanation: Confirmation checks whether the original defect was fixed; regression checks unintended consequences elsewhere.

questions.prompt: HOP migrates to a new PostgreSQL version. What should guide maintenance testing?
options: The assumption that unchanged code cannot fail
Impact analysis and risks of the migration
questions.explanation: Modifications, migration and retirement can trigger maintenance testing; scope depends on change impact and risk.

questions.prompt: An old billing system is retired and its data archived. Is testing relevant?
options: Only if the original developers remain employed
Yes; test migration, retrieval and retirement-related behavior as appropriate
Only if new features are developed
questions.explanation: Modifications, migration and retirement can trigger maintenance testing; scope depends on change impact and risk.

questions.prompt: Which HOP item can be examined with static testing?
questions.explanation: Requirements, code, test cases and other readable work products can be examined statically.

questions.prompt: Can a test plan be the subject of a review?
options: Yes, it is a work product suitable for static testing
No, only source code can be reviewed
Only after it has been deployed
questions.explanation: Requirements, code, test cases and other readable work products can be examined statically.

questions.prompt: A HOP review finds contradictory shift rules before coding. What is the main benefit?
options: Avoiding implementation and later rework based on the contradiction
Proving future code contains no defects
questions.explanation: Static testing can find ambiguities, omissions and other defects early, often reducing downstream rework.

questions.prompt: Why review acceptance criteria early?
options: Only completed code can contain useful evidence
Ambiguities can be corrected before implementation depends on them
questions.explanation: Static testing can find ambiguities, omissions and other defects early, often reducing downstream rework.

questions.prompt: Reading HOP SQL for a missing constraint is which kind of testing?
questions.explanation: Static testing examines work products without execution; dynamic testing executes software to observe behavior.

questions.prompt: Executing a mobile app and comparing actual with expected results is which kind of testing?
questions.explanation: Static testing examines work products without execution; dynamic testing executes software to observe behavior.

questions.prompt: Why show proposed HOP shift rules to managers early?
options: To discover misunderstood business needs sooner
To guarantee no later change requests
questions.explanation: Early, frequent feedback clarifies needs and reduces misunderstanding.

questions.prompt: What is a benefit of frequent customer feedback on a prototype?
options: A guarantee that every requirement is complete
No need for future acceptance testing
questions.explanation: Early, frequent feedback clarifies needs and reduces misunderstanding.

questions.prompt: HOP reviewers individually note anomalies before the review discussion. What activity is this?
questions.explanation: A review commonly includes planning, initiation, individual review, communication/analysis and fixing/reporting.

questions.prompt: After a review identifies an agreed defect, what makes the process complete?
options: Assume the meeting itself repaired it
Replace the original requirement without checking
Track fixing and report the review outcome
questions.explanation: A review commonly includes planning, initiation, individual review, communication/analysis and fixing/reporting.

questions.prompt: Who primarily facilitates a formal HOP review meeting?
questions.explanation: The moderator facilitates the review; reviewers identify anomalies; authors create and fix work products; scribes record information.

questions.prompt: Who normally records review information such as decisions and anomalies?
options: The test execution tool by definition
questions.explanation: The moderator facilitates the review; reviewers identify anomalies; authors create and fix work products; scribes record information.

questions.prompt: A HOP author leads colleagues through a specification and gathers feedback. Which review fits best?
questions.explanation: Walkthroughs are led by authors; technical reviews seek consensus and evaluate quality; inspections are the most formal review type.

questions.prompt: Which review type normally has the greatest formality with defined roles and collected metrics?
questions.explanation: Walkthroughs are led by authors; technical reviews seek consensus and evaluate quality; inspections are the most formal review type.

questions.prompt: What helps a HOP requirement review succeed?
options: Clear objectives and adequate preparation time
Using the meeting to evaluate individual staff performance
Reviewing unlimited material in one sitting
questions.explanation: Suitable participants, preparation, manageable work products, clear goals and supportive communication improve reviews.

questions.prompt: Which environment best supports effective reviews?
options: Constructive discussion focused on the work product
questions.explanation: Suitable participants, preparation, manageable work products, clear goals and supportive communication improve reviews.

questions.prompt: HOP tests are derived solely from role-permission requirements. Which technique category fits?
questions.explanation: Black-box techniques derive tests from specified behavior; white-box from structure; experience-based from knowledge of likely defects.

questions.prompt: A tester selects cases to exercise branches in source code. Which category fits?
questions.explanation: Black-box techniques derive tests from specified behavior; white-box from structure; experience-based from knowledge of likely defects.

questions.prompt: HOP accepts integer party sizes 1–100. Which set covers below-range, valid and above-range partitions?
questions.explanation: Partitions are non-overlapping sets expected to be treated similarly; include valid and invalid classes.

questions.prompt: A discount applies to ages 18–64 inclusive; other integer ages receive no discount, with below and above treated as separate partitions. Which set covers all three?
questions.explanation: Partitions are non-overlapping sets expected to be treated similarly; include valid and invalid classes.

questions.prompt: HOP accepts integer party sizes 1–100. Which set gives 2-value boundary coverage?
questions.explanation: For integer ranges, 2-value BVA exercises the values on both sides of each boundary; 3-value adds the neighboring interior value.

questions.prompt: An input accepts integers 10–20. Which set gives 3-value boundary coverage?
questions.explanation: For integer ranges, 2-value BVA exercises the values on both sides of each boundary; 3-value adds the neighboring interior value.

questions.prompt: HOP allows approval only when the user is a manager AND the request is Pending. What should happen for manager=true and Pending=false?
options: The rule has no defined outcome
questions.explanation: Each feasible rule is a combination of conditions and expected actions; full rule coverage exercises all feasible columns.

questions.prompt: A form has two independent Boolean conditions and no impossible combinations. How many rules are in the full decision table before minimization?
questions.explanation: Each feasible rule is a combination of conditions and expected actions; full rule coverage exercises all feasible columns.

questions.prompt: HOP allows Pending→Approved, Pending→Rejected and Approved→Completed. Which sequence is invalid?
questions.explanation: Tests exercise states and transitions, including prohibited transitions where relevant; visiting states alone may miss transitions.

questions.prompt: A lock permits Unlocked→Locked and Locked→Unlocked. A test visits both states using only Unlocked→Locked. What remains uncovered?
questions.explanation: Tests exercise states and transitions, including prohibited transitions where relevant; visiting states alone may miss transitions.

questions.prompt: A HOP function has 20 executable statements. Tests execute 15 distinct statements. What is statement coverage?
questions.explanation: Statement coverage counts executed executable statements; full coverage does not guarantee all branches or defects were tested.

questions.prompt: A suite executes every executable statement. What can be concluded?
options: Statement coverage is 100%, but some branches may remain untested
questions.explanation: Statement coverage counts executed executable statements; full coverage does not guarantee all branches or defects were tested.

questions.prompt: A HOP test takes the true outcome of an IF but never the false outcome. What remains untested?
questions.explanation: Branch coverage measures exercised branches; 100% branch coverage implies 100% statement coverage, but not the reverse.

questions.prompt: Tests exercise 6 of 8 control-flow branches. What is branch coverage?
questions.explanation: Branch coverage measures exercised branches; 100% branch coverage implies 100% statement coverage, but not the reverse.

questions.prompt: HOP has high functional coverage but an error-handling branch never runs in tests. What can white-box analysis add?
options: Visibility of the structural coverage gap
A guarantee that no defects remain
Automatic knowledge of all customer needs
questions.explanation: White-box testing can reveal unexercised structure; it does not reveal every omitted requirement or guarantee correctness.

questions.prompt: Why combine specification-based and structural testing?
options: Specification tests prove every branch ran
They reveal different kinds of coverage gaps
questions.explanation: White-box testing can reveal unexercised structure; it does not reveal every omitted requirement or guarantee correctness.

questions.prompt: Past HOP bugs involved double-click submissions. A tester specifically tries rapid repeated clicks. Which technique fits?
questions.explanation: Error guessing draws on knowledge of failures, developer mistakes and defects to target tests.

questions.prompt: A tester checks blank fields after recalling similar validation failures in earlier products. What guides the test?
questions.explanation: Error guessing draws on knowledge of failures, developer mistakes and defects to target tests.

questions.prompt: A tester investigates HOP mobile notifications, adapting the next check from each observation. Which approach fits?
questions.explanation: Exploratory testing combines learning, design and execution, often in timeboxed sessions guided by a charter.

questions.prompt: What makes an exploratory session more focused and reviewable?
options: A charter, timebox and session notes
questions.explanation: Exploratory testing combines learning, design and execution, often in timeboxed sessions guided by a charter.

questions.prompt: A HOP tester uses a list covering mobile layout, validation and error messages. Which technique fits?
questions.explanation: A checklist guides testing while allowing variation in how items are checked; it needs updating as experience changes.

questions.prompt: What is a limitation of a stale test checklist?
options: It may miss risks introduced by product changes
It guarantees all requirements are tested
It automatically adapts to new features
questions.explanation: A checklist guides testing while allowing variation in how items are checked; it needs updating as experience changes.

questions.prompt: Who should help refine a HOP shift-swap user story?
options: Only the person writing the final code
questions.explanation: Business, development and testing perspectives refine a user story and clarify acceptance expectations.

questions.prompt: Why discuss examples while refining a user story?
options: They guarantee the story cannot change
They expose differing interpretations and improve shared understanding
questions.explanation: Business, development and testing perspectives refine a user story and clarify acceptance expectations.

questions.prompt: HOP documents: Given a Pending request, When a manager approves, Then status is Approved. What form is this?
questions.explanation: Criteria may be scenario-oriented (Given/When/Then) or rule-oriented (a list of rules).

questions.prompt: A story lists three validation rules as acceptance conditions. What form is this?
questions.explanation: Criteria may be scenario-oriented (Given/When/Then) or rule-oriented (a list of rules).

questions.prompt: HOP says only Pending requests may be approved. Which pair of tests best derives from this rule?
options: Approve Pending succeeds; approve Rejected is denied
Approve Pending twice without checking outcomes
questions.explanation: ATDD uses agreed examples and acceptance criteria to derive tests before implementation.

questions.prompt: A story says shipping is free for totals of at least $50. Which acceptance tests best cover the rule's two outcomes?
options: Only check that the page opens
questions.explanation: ATDD uses agreed examples and acceptance criteria to derive tests before implementation.

questions.prompt: Which item belongs in a HOP test plan?
options: The test scope, approach and exit criteria
Only the final list of repaired defects
questions.explanation: A test plan communicates objectives, scope, approach, resources, schedule, risks and criteria.

questions.prompt: Why write a test plan?
options: Coordinate testing and communicate how objectives will be addressed
questions.explanation: A test plan communicates objectives, scope, approach, resources, schedule, risks and criteria.

questions.prompt: How can a tester add value to HOP iteration planning?
options: Identify test effort and clarify acceptance criteria
Promise all features are equally easy to test
questions.explanation: Testers clarify testability, risks, effort and acceptance criteria during iteration and release planning.

questions.prompt: Which contribution helps release planning?
options: Highlighting test dependencies and quality risks
questions.explanation: Testers clarify testability, risks, effort and acceptance criteria during iteration and release planning.

questions.prompt: HOP requires a working test environment before system testing starts. What is this?
questions.explanation: Entry criteria establish prerequisites; exit criteria define completion conditions, including residual risks.

questions.prompt: The agreed release condition requires all critical tests passed and no open critical defects. What is this?
options: An entry condition for writing requirements
questions.explanation: Entry criteria establish prerequisites; exit criteria define completion conditions, including residual risks.

questions.prompt: HOP test effort estimates are optimistic 4h, most likely 7h, pessimistic 16h. What is the three-point estimate?
questions.explanation: Three-point estimation uses (optimistic + 4×most likely + pessimistic)/6; estimates remain uncertain.

questions.prompt: A testing task has estimates 2h, 5h and 8h. What is the three-point weighted estimate?
questions.explanation: Three-point estimation uses (optimistic + 4×most likely + pessimistic)/6; estimates remain uncertain.

questions.prompt: HOP's high-risk payment test B requires setup test A; low-risk visual test C is independent. Which order best respects both dependency and risk?
questions.explanation: Risk, coverage and requirements guide priority, but prerequisites can constrain execution order.

questions.prompt: T1 covers requirements A/B, T2 covers B/C, T3 covers D. After T1, which choice maximizes additional requirement coverage if all have equal priority and cost?
options: Either T2 or T3, each adds one uncovered requirement
questions.explanation: Risk, coverage and requirements guide priority, but prerequisites can constrain execution order.

questions.prompt: Which distribution best reflects a test pyramid?
options: One component test and thousands of UI tests
Equal numbers are mandatory at every level
Many component tests, fewer integration tests, few end-to-end tests
questions.explanation: The test pyramid favors many small fast tests at lower levels and fewer slower end-to-end tests.

questions.prompt: Why does the test pyramid favor lower-level automated tests?
options: They test every user journey by themselves
They generally provide faster and more focused feedback
questions.explanation: The test pyramid favors many small fast tests at lower levels and fewer slower end-to-end tests.

questions.prompt: Which quadrant best fits business-facing examples that guide HOP development?
questions.explanation: Quadrants combine business/technology focus with supporting the team/critiquing the product; they are not a required execution order.

questions.prompt: Performance and security checks critique the product from a technology perspective. Which quadrant fits?
questions.explanation: Quadrants combine business/technology focus with supporting the team/critiquing the product; they are not a required execution order.

questions.prompt: Using likelihood×impact, a HOP risk has likelihood 3 and impact 4. What is its risk level?
questions.explanation: Risk level depends on likelihood and impact; numerical multiplication is one possible quantitative approach.

questions.prompt: Which two attributes determine risk level?
questions.explanation: Risk level depends on likelihood and impact; numerical multiplication is one possible quantitative approach.

questions.prompt: HOP may calculate invoice tax incorrectly. What kind of risk is this?
questions.explanation: Product risks concern quality; project risks concern project delivery and management.

questions.prompt: A test environment supplier may deliver two weeks late. What kind of risk is this?
questions.explanation: Product risks concern quality; project risks concern project delivery and management.

questions.prompt: HOP permission failures have high impact and likelihood. How should this affect testing?
options: Test permissions last regardless of other factors
Assume all features need identical effort
Increase appropriate scope and rigor for permissions
questions.explanation: Product risk analysis identifies and assesses risks to guide test scope, effort, techniques and priority.

questions.prompt: Why estimate product risk before choosing test depth?
options: It helps allocate limited testing effort where failures matter most
It proves exactly which defects exist
questions.explanation: Product risk analysis identifies and assesses risks to guide test scope, effort, techniques and priority.

questions.prompt: HOP cannot fully test a risky feature before launch. What is a valid risk response?
options: Discuss residual risk and consider deferring the feature
questions.explanation: Risk control may mitigate through testing, transfer, accept or avoid risks; remaining risk should be monitored and communicated.

questions.prompt: A team adds focused tests and monitors a high-risk transaction. What is it doing?
questions.explanation: Risk control may mitigate through testing, transfer, accept or avoid risks; remaining risk should be monitored and communicated.

questions.prompt: Which metric directly shows HOP test execution progress?
options: Executed tests compared with planned tests
questions.explanation: Useful metrics include execution progress, coverage, defects, effort and residual risk; no single count proves quality.

questions.prompt: Which measure can help describe remaining test scope?
questions.explanation: Useful metrics include execution progress, coverage, defects, effort and residual risk; no single count proves quality.

questions.prompt: What should a HOP test completion report communicate?
options: A guarantee of no future defects
questions.explanation: Progress reports support ongoing decisions; completion reports summarize outcomes and remaining risks.

questions.prompt: Which report best supports an ongoing decision to adjust test resources?
questions.explanation: Progress reports support ongoing decisions; completion reports summarize outcomes and remaining risks.

questions.prompt: HOP's restaurant owner needs a release decision. What is the most suitable status summary?
options: Every raw test log with no summary
Business impact, key results and remaining risks
questions.explanation: Communication should be timely and suited to stakeholders, using relevant detail and channels.

questions.prompt: Developers need to reproduce a failing API check. What communication is most useful?
options: A vague statement that it is broken
Specific steps, inputs, environment and observed results
questions.explanation: Communication should be timely and suited to stakeholders, using relevant detail and channels.

questions.prompt: HOP tests pass on a build, but nobody recorded its version. What is missing?
options: Configuration identification linking tests to the tested build
questions.explanation: Configuration management identifies versions, baselines and controlled changes so test evidence is reproducible.

questions.prompt: Why baseline test data and scripts with a release?
options: To reproduce results against known versions
To prevent any future software change
questions.explanation: Configuration management identifies versions, baselines and controlled changes so test evidence is reproducible.

questions.prompt: Which HOP defect report is most actionable?
options: Build 8, manager login: approve Pending request; expected Approved, actual 500; request trace attached
The developers did a bad job
questions.explanation: Useful reports include clear summary, environment, steps, expected/actual results and supporting evidence; severity and priority differ.

questions.prompt: Which report best supports reproducing a mobile display defect?
options: Device/browser/build, steps, expected layout, actual clipping and screenshot
questions.explanation: Useful reports include clear summary, environment, steps, expected/actual results and supporting evidence; severity and priority differ.

questions.prompt: HOP wants repeatable execution of API checks after commits. What tool category fits?
questions.explanation: Tools support management, static analysis, design, execution and other activities; select based on the required capability.

questions.prompt: HOP wants to detect code issues without running the application. What tool capability fits?
questions.explanation: Tools support management, static analysis, design, execution and other activities; select based on the required capability.

questions.prompt: Which is a realistic automation risk for HOP?
options: Maintenance effort when the application changes
questions.explanation: Automation can improve repeatability and speed; setup, maintenance and unrealistic expectations are risks.

questions.prompt: Which is a typical benefit of test automation?
questions.explanation: Automation can improve repeatability and speed; setup, maintenance and unrealistic expectations are risks.

questions.prompt: A HOP release has passed its planned tests but still has two known low-impact defects. What is the MOST appropriate testing contribution to the release decision?
options: Report the results and residual risks to the decision-maker
Authorize release solely because the planned cases ran
Require defect count to be zero regardless of the agreed criteria
Extend testing indefinitely until every input combination is checked
questions.explanation: Testing provides evidence for a decision; completing tests is not itself proof that all risk is acceptable.

questions.prompt: In a whole team approach, a developer helps a tester design a difficult integration check. Which statement is MOST accurate?
options: The tester has transferred all responsibility for quality to the developer
The developer should avoid test design to preserve tester independence
The test becomes an acceptance test because two roles collaborated
Sharing expertise supports the team's collective responsibility for quality
questions.explanation: Whole team collaboration combines skills. It neither removes specialist responsibilities nor changes the test level automatically.

questions.prompt: An unclear date-format requirement leads a programmer to assume month/day order. The code stores the wrong date, and a manager sees a shift on the wrong day. Which pairing is correct?
options: Programmer assumption: defect; wrong code: error
Displayed wrong day: error; programmer assumption: failure
Programmer assumption: error; wrong stored-date logic: defect
Unclear requirement: failure; displayed wrong day: root cause
questions.explanation: The person's mistaken action is an error; a flaw in the work product is a defect; incorrect observed behavior is a failure.

questions.prompt: A HOP team finds most defects in a small number of modules. It plans additional tests in those modules while retaining risk-based checks elsewhere. Which principle MOST directly supports the focus?
questions.explanation: Defect clustering describes concentration of defects. It supports focused attention without proving that other modules are safe.

questions.prompt: After identifying test conditions, a tester prepares concrete input data, expected outcomes and coverage targets. Another tester then assembles executable suites. Which distinction is correct?
options: Both are debugging because expected outcomes are specified
The first is mainly test design; the second is test implementation
Both are test monitoring because they precede execution
The first is test completion; the second is test analysis
questions.explanation: Test design elaborates how to test conditions. Implementation creates the executable procedures, suites and supporting environment/data.

questions.prompt: A manager needs evidence of what actually happened during yesterday's test run. Which testware is MOST useful?
options: A list of conditions planned for the next release
The testing policy describing long-term principles
A preliminary estimate of test effort
Execution logs with actual results and linked defect reports
questions.explanation: Execution records show observed results. Plans and conditions describe intent and cannot establish what happened in a completed run.

questions.prompt: A legal retention rule changes. HOP has many tests, each linked to requirements and results. What benefit does this traceability provide FIRST?
options: Prove all existing results remain valid under the new rule
Eliminate the need to discuss the change with stakeholders
Identify tests whose basis changed and assess the impact
Automatically rewrite all affected test cases correctly
questions.explanation: Traceability helps locate affected testware and assess change impact; it does not automatically update tests or validate old results.

questions.prompt: A separate test team finds defects missed by developers, but handoffs are slowing feedback. What is the BEST response?
options: Keep the additional perspective while improving collaboration and communication
Remove all developer testing because the separate team is independent
Assume independent testing is ineffective because delays occurred
Require testers to communicate only after a complete release
questions.explanation: Independence can uncover different defects, while isolation can harm communication. The two effects should be managed together.

questions.prompt: Which practice remains useful in sequential, iterative and incremental delivery?
options: Complete all acceptance testing before requirements discussions
Use only one test level to avoid duplicate effort
Review draft work products as soon as they are available
Require the final system build before identifying any test conditions
questions.explanation: Early review and early test analysis are useful across lifecycles; delivery structure changes their timing and scope.

questions.prompt: A team writes a failing component test, makes it pass with implementation, and then improves the code structure. Which approach is illustrated?
options: Exploratory testing guided by a charter
Acceptance test-driven development focused on business examples
questions.explanation: The failing component test, implementation and refactoring cycle is characteristic of TDD. ATDD and BDD emphasize different kinds of examples.

questions.prompt: HOP's invoice component works in isolation. A test then checks communication between HOP and an external payment provider. Which test level BEST describes the latter?
options: User acceptance testing merely because payment is business-related
Component integration testing confined to internal units
questions.explanation: System integration testing focuses on interfaces with other systems and external services, rather than interactions among isolated internal components.

questions.prompt: A repaired discount defect is checked with its original failing example. Tests then check invoice totals for other discounts. Which description is BEST?
options: All tests are confirmation because they concern invoices
All tests are regression because the software changed
The first is debugging; the others are static testing
The first confirms the fix; the others check for regressions
questions.explanation: Confirmation targets the repaired defect. Regression checks for adverse effects of the change, including in the same subsystem.

questions.prompt: A retrospective recommends better test-data setup. At the next retrospective, setup still consumes the same time and nobody owns the action. What is the MOST useful next step?
options: Declare the improvement successful because it was discussed
Stop discussing testing because retrospectives concern development only
Assign responsibility and a measurable follow-up for the improvement
Record the same recommendation without changing its handling
questions.explanation: Retrospectives produce improvement actions that need ownership and evaluation, rather than recommendations without follow-through.

questions.prompt: A team reviews HOP acceptance criteria and develops tests before implementation. It also retains end-to-end checks before release. Which statement is correct?
options: It is shift right because the release still receives testing
This is shift left without assuming that early checks replace later testing
It is not shift left because end-to-end checks still exist
Shift left requires replacing every later test with static analysis
questions.explanation: Shift left moves suitable activities earlier while preserving appropriate later test levels and feedback.

questions.prompt: Which pair can both be examined by static testing?
options: Only API requests after they have been executed
A user story and a test script
Only a running application and its response time
Only memory usage and throughput measurements
questions.explanation: Static testing can inspect requirements and testware without executing the software. Runtime measurements are produced by dynamic activity.

questions.prompt: During a review, Ana creates the work product, Ben facilitates the meeting, and Cara records findings. Which mapping is correct?
options: Ana moderator; Ben scribe; Cara author
Ana scribe; Ben author; Cara reviewer only
Ana test manager; Ben author; Cara moderator
Ana author; Ben moderator; Cara scribe
questions.explanation: The author owns the work product, the moderator facilitates, and the scribe records review information.

questions.prompt: A review identifies an unreachable-code defect, while an executed test reveals an incorrect API response. Which comparison is correct?
options: The review observed a failure; the run can reveal only document defects
Static and dynamic testing cannot find related issues
Static testing found a defect directly; dynamic testing revealed a failure
Both observations required executing the defective statement
questions.explanation: Static examination can find defects without execution. Dynamic testing observes behavior that can reveal failures caused by defects.

questions.prompt: A HOP team needs a structured review with formal roles and metrics to evaluate the process. Which review type is MOST appropriate?
options: An author-led walkthrough with no required formal metrics
questions.explanation: Inspection is the most formal review type, with defined roles and metrics; the other choices serve different or less formal purposes.

questions.prompt: A tester derives checks from requirements, another from branch structure, and a third from recurring defect patterns. Which order of technique categories is correct?
questions.explanation: Requirements describe externally specified behavior; branch structure is internal; recurring defects supply experience-based test ideas.

questions.prompt: A function has an IF with no ELSE. One test takes the true outcome and executes every statement. Which claim is justified?
options: 100% statement coverage can coexist with incomplete branch coverage
100% statement coverage proves the false outcome was exercised
The IF condition is not part of structural testing
Incomplete branch coverage means no statement was executed
questions.explanation: Taking the true outcome can execute every statement while leaving the false outcome unexercised.

questions.prompt: A test suite achieves full branch coverage of a module. Which implication is valid for the covered module?
options: It covers every possible path through repeated loops
It proves all specified business behavior was implemented
It guarantees no boundary-related defects remain
It also achieves full statement coverage, but not proof of correctness
questions.explanation: Full branch coverage implies statement coverage; path combinations, omitted functionality and incorrect computations can still escape it.

questions.prompt: After several field reports about stale sessions, a tester designs checks around token expiry and replay based on those reports. Which technique MOST directly motivated the cases?
options: Random testing with no defect knowledge
Decision-table derivation from enumerated Boolean rules
questions.explanation: Knowledge of prior failures and likely mistakes guides error guessing. A test can later also contribute to other coverage goals.

questions.prompt: A tester has a 45-minute charter to investigate HOP mobile recovery after a network interruption. Observations determine the next actions. What makes this exploratory testing?
options: The absence of written test cases makes results unnecessary
It must avoid using knowledge from previous defects
Learning, test design and execution evolve together within a focused session
All test steps were fixed before the session began
questions.explanation: Exploration combines learning, design and execution, and can still use charters, notes and previous experience.

questions.prompt: A HOP story states three rules: only managers approve, only Pending requests are eligible, and approval records a timestamp. How are these acceptance criteria expressed?
questions.explanation: A list of declarative acceptance rules is rule-oriented; scenarios express particular contexts, actions and outcomes.

questions.prompt: HOP accepts a whole-number shift length from 2 through 12 hours. Inputs below 2, within the range, and above 12 are separate partitions. Which additional input is needed after tests at 2 and 8 to cover every partition with the fewest additions?
questions.explanation: Both existing inputs exercise the valid partition. Representatives of both invalid partitions are still required.

questions.prompt: HOP accepts integer notice days from 3 through 14. Existing tests use 3 and 14. Which additions complete 2-value boundary coverage?
questions.explanation: Two-value boundary analysis includes the valid boundary and the nearest invalid value on each side: 2,3 and 14,15.

questions.prompt: A discount is allowed only for a member whose order is at least $30. Tests already cover member/large order, member/small order and nonmember/large order. Which rule is missing from a full four-rule table?
options: Member with a large order; discount
Nonmember with a large order; discount
Member with a small order; discount
Nonmember with a small order; no discount
questions.explanation: Two independent Boolean conditions give four combinations. The untested false/false combination must produce no discount.

questions.prompt: A ticket supports Draft→Submitted, Submitted→Approved, Submitted→Rejected and Rejected→Draft. Tests cover Draft→Submitted→Approved and Draft→Submitted→Rejected. Which transition remains uncovered?
questions.explanation: The two tests cover three of four valid transitions. Reopening a rejected ticket is the remaining transition.

questions.prompt: HOP accepts a shift swap only when both employees consent. Which test set BEST derives from that acceptance rule?
options: Both consent: accepted; both consent again: accepted
One consents: accepted; neither consents: accepted
Only inspect whether the consent button is visible
Both consent: accepted; only one consents: not accepted; neither consents: not accepted
questions.explanation: Acceptance tests should cover the rule's accepted and rejected outcomes, including partial consent, rather than only the happy path.

questions.prompt: Which change is most consistent with the test pyramid while preserving important user-flow checks?
options: Remove end-to-end testing because component tests exist
Move suitable logic checks to component tests and retain a smaller set of end-to-end flows
Replace all component checks with UI journeys
Require every automated test to access production services
questions.explanation: The pyramid favors many focused lower-level tests and fewer broader tests, not elimination of all high-level coverage.

questions.prompt: An agreed test phase may begin when its environment is available and end when required coverage is met and residual risks are accepted. Which mapping is correct?
options: Environment availability is exit; coverage is entry
Both are entry because they appear in the plan
Both are defects because they constrain execution
Environment availability is entry; coverage and accepted risk are exit
questions.explanation: Entry criteria define readiness to begin; exit criteria define completion conditions and may include assessed residual risk.

questions.prompt: A tester conducts business-facing exploratory testing to critique the completed product. Which quadrant is the BEST match?
questions.explanation: Q3 is business-facing and critiques the product. Q2 supports the team with business examples; Q4 critiques technology-facing qualities.

questions.prompt: Which pair correctly distinguishes a product risk from a project risk?
options: Late vendor delivery; missing access control
Insufficient budget; lost customer data caused by a software failure
Incorrect tax calculation; unavailable test environment delaying work
questions.explanation: Incorrect product behavior is a product risk; resource, schedule and delivery problems are project risks.

questions.prompt: A HOP release decision needs a concise view of achieved coverage, unresolved defects and accepted deviations from the plan. Which report is MOST suitable?
options: A test procedure containing execution steps only
An unprioritized collection of raw logs only
A defect report describing just one failure
questions.explanation: A completion report summarizes the test effort and outcomes for stakeholders, including deviations and residual risks.

questions.prompt: Two testers obtain different results because they unknowingly use different rule-file versions. Which action BEST supports repeatability?
options: Require both testers to memorize the expected outputs
Delete earlier results whenever a file changes
Identify and baseline the build, rule file, test data and scripts used in each run
Record only the date of the meeting discussing the result
questions.explanation: Configuration management controls and identifies relevant versions so that test evidence can be reproduced and compared.

questions.prompt: A team historically needs 20 test hours for every 80 development hours on comparable work. Using that ratio, what test estimate fits 120 development hours?
questions.explanation: The historical ratio is 20/80 = 0.25. Multiplying 120 by 0.25 gives 30 test hours, subject to comparability and uncertainty.

questions.prompt: HOP tests A, B and C have equal execution cost. A covers risks worth 5 points, B covers 9, and C covers 3. B can run only after A. Which order best respects dependency and then risk priority?
questions.explanation: The dependency forces A before B. After A, higher-risk B should precede C under the stated priority model.

questions.prompt: A bug report says: 'HOP build 12, Chrome 130, open an approved request and click Complete; expected Completed; actual stays Approved.' What addition would MOST help investigation?
options: A priority value without any supporting evidence
Relevant request identifier or sanitized data and a response/log attachment
The reporter's opinion of the developer's skill
A promise that the defect affects every browser
questions.explanation: The report already supplies steps and expected/actual behavior. Reproducible data and evidence make investigation more effective without unsupported generalizations.

questions.prompt: HOP needs to link requirements, test cases, execution results and defects for status reporting. Which tool capability is MOST relevant?
questions.explanation: Test management tools organize and link testing artifacts and status; execution or analysis tools serve other primary needs.

questions.prompt: A team buys an automation tool but budgets no time for training or script maintenance. Which risk is MOST likely?
options: The tool will remove the need to interpret failures
All exploratory tests must become impossible
Underestimating the effort needed to introduce and sustain automation
questions.explanation: Realistic automation adoption includes learning, integration, maintenance and result analysis; buying a tool does not remove those costs.

concepts.intuitive: Find evidence for a release decision
concepts.lesson: Testing supplies information and reduces risk; it cannot prove the absence of every defect.

concepts.intuitive: Finding the problem versus fixing its cause
concepts.lesson: Testing reveals defects or failures; debugging diagnoses causes and removes defects.

concepts.intuitive: Catch costly problems before customers do
concepts.lesson: Testing helps uncover defects and informs decisions about quality and risk.

concepts.intuitive: Improve the process that produces the software
concepts.lesson: QA is process-oriented and preventive; testing evaluates work products as quality control.

concepts.intuitive: Mistake, faulty code, observed wrong behavior
concepts.lesson: A human error can introduce a defect; executing that defect may cause a failure. A root cause is the underlying reason.

concepts.intuitive: Passing checks does not prove the product is useful
concepts.lesson: Testing shows defects can exist, not that none remain. Exhaustive testing is generally impossible; tests must adapt and reflect user needs.

concepts.intuitive: Decide what to test before deciding how
concepts.lesson: Analysis identifies testable features and conditions; design derives test cases; implementation prepares procedures and data.

concepts.intuitive: Choose tests that fit this product
concepts.lesson: Domain, risks, stakeholders, lifecycle, constraints and technology affect test activities and their formality.

concepts.intuitive: The work products used to plan and run tests
concepts.lesson: Test conditions, cases, data, scripts, logs and reports support different testing activities.

concepts.intuitive: Link a requirement to its checks and results
concepts.lesson: Traceability supports coverage evaluation, change impact analysis and clear status reporting.

concepts.intuitive: Coordinating testing versus carrying it out
concepts.lesson: Test management coordinates planning and control; the testing role performs technical test activities. One person may hold both roles.

concepts.intuitive: Ask clear questions and communicate evidence
concepts.lesson: Analytical thinking, curiosity, attention to detail and constructive communication help testing.

concepts.intuitive: Quality is a shared responsibility
concepts.lesson: People with the needed skills collaborate and share responsibility for quality; this does not remove specialist skills.

concepts.intuitive: Fresh eyes find different problems
concepts.lesson: Independent testers bring different assumptions, but separation can create communication barriers and reduce shared ownership.

concepts.intuitive: Testing follows how delivery is organized
concepts.lesson: Lifecycle choices influence timing, scope, documentation and feedback; testing remains relevant across lifecycles.

concepts.intuitive: Start relevant testing early in every lifecycle
concepts.lesson: Every development activity has a corresponding testing activity; analysis and design begin early and tests align with objectives.

concepts.intuitive: Specify tests before implementation
concepts.lesson: TDD, ATDD and BDD are test-first approaches with different emphases.

concepts.intuitive: Fast delivery needs fast quality feedback
concepts.lesson: DevOps supports collaboration, CI/CD and automated feedback but does not eliminate manual testing or risk.

concepts.intuitive: Find issues earlier without abandoning later checks
concepts.lesson: Shift left moves testing earlier, such as reviewing requirements and running early tests; later testing is still needed.

concepts.intuitive: Use experience to improve the next iteration
concepts.lesson: Retrospectives identify improvements, assign actions and evaluate whether they work.

concepts.intuitive: Check components, connections and the whole product
concepts.lesson: Component tests focus on isolated parts; integration tests on interactions; system tests on the whole system; acceptance tests on business needs.

concepts.intuitive: What quality aspect are we checking?
concepts.lesson: Functional tests assess what the system does; non-functional tests assess quality characteristics such as performance or usability.

concepts.intuitive: Retest the fix, then check what else changed
concepts.lesson: Confirmation checks whether the original defect was fixed; regression checks unintended consequences elsewhere.

concepts.intuitive: Check changes to an existing system
concepts.lesson: Modifications, migration and retirement can trigger maintenance testing; scope depends on change impact and risk.

concepts.intuitive: Review things without executing software
concepts.lesson: Requirements, code, test cases and other readable work products can be examined statically.

concepts.intuitive: Find defects before they become runtime failures
concepts.lesson: Static testing can find ambiguities, omissions and other defects early, often reducing downstream rework.

concepts.intuitive: Inspect the artifact versus run the software
concepts.lesson: Static testing examines work products without execution; dynamic testing executes software to observe behavior.

concepts.intuitive: Check shared understanding before it is expensive to change
concepts.lesson: Early, frequent feedback clarifies needs and reduces misunderstanding.

concepts.intuitive: Prepare, inspect, discuss and follow up
concepts.lesson: A review commonly includes planning, initiation, individual review, communication/analysis and fixing/reporting.

concepts.intuitive: The moderator helps the review work
concepts.lesson: The moderator facilitates the review; reviewers identify anomalies; authors create and fix work products; scribes record information.

concepts.intuitive: Choose the review form to fit the goal
concepts.lesson: Walkthroughs are led by authors; technical reviews seek consensus and evaluate quality; inspections are the most formal review type.

concepts.intuitive: Clear goals and a constructive environment
concepts.lesson: Suitable participants, preparation, manageable work products, clear goals and supportive communication improve reviews.

concepts.intuitive: Behavior, structure or experience guides the tests
concepts.lesson: Black-box techniques derive tests from specified behavior; white-box from structure; experience-based from knowledge of likely defects.

concepts.intuitive: Choose representatives of groups expected to behave alike
concepts.lesson: Partitions are non-overlapping sets expected to be treated similarly; include valid and invalid classes.

concepts.intuitive: Test the edges where behavior changes
concepts.lesson: For integer ranges, 2-value BVA exercises the values on both sides of each boundary; 3-value adds the neighboring interior value.

concepts.intuitive: Cover meaningful combinations of conditions
concepts.lesson: Each feasible rule is a combination of conditions and expected actions; full rule coverage exercises all feasible columns.

concepts.intuitive: Behavior depends on current state and event
concepts.lesson: Tests exercise states and transitions, including prohibited transitions where relevant; visiting states alone may miss transitions.

concepts.intuitive: How many executable statements ran?
concepts.lesson: Statement coverage counts executed executable statements; full coverage does not guarantee all branches or defects were tested.

concepts.intuitive: Exercise the control-flow alternatives
concepts.lesson: Branch coverage measures exercised branches; 100% branch coverage implies 100% statement coverage, but not the reverse.

concepts.intuitive: See structural gaps that behavior tests may miss
concepts.lesson: White-box testing can reveal unexercised structure; it does not reveal every omitted requirement or guarantee correctness.

concepts.intuitive: Use experience with likely mistakes
concepts.lesson: Error guessing draws on knowledge of failures, developer mistakes and defects to target tests.

concepts.intuitive: Learn, design and execute together
concepts.lesson: Exploratory testing combines learning, design and execution, often in timeboxed sessions guided by a charter.

concepts.intuitive: Use a concise list of things to check
concepts.lesson: A checklist guides testing while allowing variation in how items are checked; it needs updating as experience changes.

concepts.intuitive: Agree on the story through several perspectives
concepts.lesson: Business, development and testing perspectives refine a user story and clarify acceptance expectations.

concepts.intuitive: Make the conditions for acceptance explicit
concepts.lesson: Criteria may be scenario-oriented (Given/When/Then) or rule-oriented (a list of rules).

concepts.intuitive: Derive acceptance tests before building
concepts.lesson: ATDD uses agreed examples and acceptance criteria to derive tests before implementation.

concepts.intuitive: Agree scope, approach, people and schedule
concepts.lesson: A test plan communicates objectives, scope, approach, resources, schedule, risks and criteria.

concepts.intuitive: Bring test effort and risk into delivery decisions
concepts.lesson: Testers clarify testability, risks, effort and acceptance criteria during iteration and release planning.

concepts.intuitive: Ready to start versus ready to finish
concepts.lesson: Entry criteria establish prerequisites; exit criteria define completion conditions, including residual risks.

concepts.intuitive: Estimate effort using evidence and uncertainty
concepts.lesson: Three-point estimation uses (optimistic + 4×most likely + pessimistic)/6; estimates remain uncertain.

concepts.intuitive: Run valuable checks while respecting dependencies
concepts.lesson: Risk, coverage and requirements guide priority, but prerequisites can constrain execution order.

concepts.intuitive: Many fast lower-level checks, fewer broad checks
concepts.lesson: The test pyramid favors many small fast tests at lower levels and fewer slower end-to-end tests.

concepts.intuitive: Organize tests by purpose and perspective
concepts.lesson: Quadrants combine business/technology focus with supporting the team/critiquing the product; they are not a required execution order.

concepts.intuitive: Combine how likely and how damaging
concepts.lesson: Risk level depends on likelihood and impact; numerical multiplication is one possible quantitative approach.

concepts.intuitive: The product may fail versus delivery may slip
concepts.lesson: Product risks concern quality; project risks concern project delivery and management.

concepts.intuitive: Use risks to decide depth and scope
concepts.lesson: Product risk analysis identifies and assesses risks to guide test scope, effort, techniques and priority.

concepts.intuitive: Reduce, monitor or consciously accept risk
concepts.lesson: Risk control may mitigate through testing, transfer, accept or avoid risks; remaining risk should be monitored and communicated.

concepts.intuitive: Measure progress and quality evidence
concepts.lesson: Useful metrics include execution progress, coverage, defects, effort and residual risk; no single count proves quality.

concepts.intuitive: Tell the audience what they need to decide
concepts.lesson: Progress reports support ongoing decisions; completion reports summarize outcomes and remaining risks.

concepts.intuitive: Adapt the evidence to the audience
concepts.lesson: Communication should be timely and suited to stakeholders, using relevant detail and channels.

concepts.intuitive: Know exactly what was tested
concepts.lesson: Configuration management identifies versions, baselines and controlled changes so test evidence is reproducible.

concepts.intuitive: Give enough evidence for someone else to reproduce it
concepts.lesson: Useful reports include clear summary, environment, steps, expected/actual results and supporting evidence; severity and priority differ.

concepts.intuitive: Choose tools for the task they support
concepts.lesson: Tools support management, static analysis, design, execution and other activities; select based on the required capability.

concepts.intuitive: Automation saves repetition but needs maintenance
concepts.lesson: Automation can improve repeatability and speed; setup, maintenance and unrealistic expectations are risks.
